pathogen_type: Ascomycete fungus; primarily a foliar pathogen

early_symptoms: Small oval to elongated pale green, grey-green, or water-soaked spots
Initial spots usually begin on lower leaves
mature_lesions: Long elliptical, spindle-shaped, or cigar-shaped lesions
Lesions are typically slender, oblong, and tapered at both ends
Lesions run broadly parallel to leaf veins or leaf margins
Typical reported length in Egyptian research is about 3–15 cm
sporulation_features: Dark grey to olive-grey dusty or sooty fungal sporulation in mature lesions
Sporulation is especially visible on the underside of infected leaves under humid conditions
advanced_symptoms: Individual lesions enlarge and merge into irregular areas of dead tissue
Extensive leaf blighting, drying, brittleness, and premature leaf death
Severe foliage damage can resemble frost injury
image_annotation_targets: dark/sooty sporulation at lesion centres or undersides
lesion coalescence and percentage of dead leaf area

symptoms: brittle, frost-like foliage in severe infections

lesion_dimensions.note: Size varies with cultivar, infection timing, and environment.

distribution_on_plant: Usually starts on lower leaves and progresses upward; late infections may be distributed throughout the canopy.
progression: Initial water-soaked or pale spots appear on lower leaves.
Spots elongate into grey-green, elliptical or cigar-shaped lesions.
Lesions become tan/straw-coloured and may develop dark sporulation, particularly in humid conditions.
Lesions expand and coalesce, destroying photosynthetic tissue and causing whole-leaf or extensive canopy blighting.

egypt_distribution_and_epidemiology.seasonal_pattern: Most commonly reported in late-summer or off-season maize in the northern and north-western Delta.
favourable_field_conditions: High humidity and prolonged leaf wetness/dew
Moderate temperatures; an Egyptian field study cites 18–27 °C and 6–18 hours of free water on leaves as favourable for infection
Sprinkler irrigation in newly reclaimed lands can increase field moisture and disease incidence
Late-summer planting dates that coincide with suitable humidity and infection conditions
egypt_distribution_and_epidemiology.egyptian_impact_evidence: Egyptian studies report grain-yield losses of about 30% or more in the Northern Delta under favourable disease conditions; losses are strongly dependent on cultivar, disease severity, and timing.

egypt_specific_research.location: Nubaria and Sakha Agricultural Research Stations, Egypt
egypt_specific_research.finding: Natural and artificial infection trials evaluated Egyptian maize lines and hybrids. Sids 63, Giza 602, and Giza 628 were resistant in both locations, while Nubaria 39 and Gemmiza 18 were susceptible.

egypt_specific_research.location: Kafr El-Sheikh University research farm, Egypt
egypt_specific_research.finding: Inoculated trials during 2020 and 2021 found lower disease severity in SC10 and SC176 than in the Balady variety; disease severity was higher with fresh animal manure than with stored/decomposed manure.

Egyptian breeding research described the characteristic 3–15 cm grey-green to tan cigar-shaped lesions and grey sporulation, mainly on lesion undersides, and evaluated resistance using field disease nurseries.

similar_diseases_for_visual_differential.distinguishing_visual_hint: Usually smaller, more uniformly oval or rectangular lesions; NLB is more characteristically long, cigar-shaped, and tapered.
More rectangular, vein-limited grey lesions; NLB lesions are generally broader, longer, and spindle/cigar-shaped.
Rust produces many small raised orange-brown pustules rather than long necrotic cigar lesions.

diagnostic_caution: Visual symptoms are strongly suggestive but not definitive. Confirm doubtful cases by microscopic examination of conidia/sporulation or laboratory isolation/molecular identification, especially where Southern corn leaf blight or gray leaf spot is also present.
